title: Efficient Influence Function for Hidden Multi-Level Treatments with Continuous Outcomes
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; projected paper-score ceiling 6.4 < 7.4 and not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: Canonicality is proved only at the specially defined two-sided pathwise-interior laws satisfying quantitative feature, posterior-Gram, and projection-Gram separation.
The cross-fitted limit theorem is conditional on aggregate nuisance and derived-operator rates, and the proposed spline product-likelihood estimator is not proved to satisfy them.
The maternal-smoking use case remains prospective and supplies neither verification of the identifying assumptions nor an empirical demonstration.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed an exact finite-cell projector, a conditional differential-score lift, a support-cleaned coherent estimator, quadratic-bias control, and a nonbinary continuous witness. The result fell below the field floor because canonicality is confined to a quantitatively separated pathwise-interior stratum and the proposed nuisance-fitting route was not proved to attain the rates required for efficient inference. A re-raised project would need an end-to-end feasible nuisance construction on a materially broader anchor class, together with verified applied assumptions or evidence.
tldr: For fixed \(K\geq3\), the exact continuous-outcome canonical gradient remains the product-bridge score minus the pointwise \(K^2\)-cell projection and one conditional Gram correction.  The implementable estimator now fits one raw product law, threshold-cleans and renormalizes both measurement matrices without a support oracle or beta-min condition, and forms every bridge and operator from that cleaned law.  If the raw uniform errors are \(o_P(\tau_{S,n})\), true-zero cells are recovered exactly; under the displayed cleaned product rates, cross-fitting attains the efficient joint Gaussian and maximum-\(t\) limits.  Proving the named global spline product-likelihood rates remains an explicit open question.
gap: The binary hidden-treatment literature characterizes efficiency but computes the continuous-outcome correction through the specific partition-dependent sequence in Supplement S8.2, while the categorical product-bridge literature establishes validity without observed-data canonicality. Existing continuous three-proxy full-law identification does not supply the uniformly bounded derivative inverse needed for tangent completeness.
fill: The project proves the missing DQM tangent-completeness theorem through a constant-\(X\) finite-feature inverse followed by a measurable conditional extension, derives the exact \(D\)-orthogonal finite projector onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\) for fixed \(K\geq3\), proves its Bayes-equivalent posterior representation, relates its binary restriction to the published Supplement S8.2 outcome-partition sequence, supplies an observable strict-gain criterion for adjacent exposure contrasts and an explicit non-binary witness, and attaches coherent cross-fitted inference under explicit nuisance products.
